sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavaḥ punaḥ vyahanat pāṇḍavīṃ senām āsurīm iva vṛtrahā
english: At that very moment Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, once more smote the army of the Pāṇḍavas, as the slayer of Vṛtra smites the host of the Asuras.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānā bhīṣmeṇa pāñcālāḥ somakaiḥ saha āryāṃ yuddhe matiṃ kṛtvā bhīṣmam evābhidudruvuḥ
english: Cut down by Bhīṣma, the Pāñcālas together with the Somakas, fixing their noble resolve upon the battle, rushed straight at Bhīṣma himself.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnamukhāś cāpi pārthāḥ śāṃtanavaṃ raṇe abhyadhāvañ jigīṣantas tava putrasya vāhinīm
english: And the sons of Pṛthā too, led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, charged at the son of Śaṃtanu in the fray, eager to overcome the host of your son.

sanskrit: tathaiva tāvakā rājan bhīṣmadroṇamukhāḥ parān abhyadhāvanta vegena tato yuddham avartata
english: In the same way your warriors, O king, led by Bhīṣma and Droṇa, rushed against the foe with great speed, and thereupon the battle was joined.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca virāṭo 'tha tribhir bāṇair bhīṣmam ārchan mahāratham vivyādha turagāṃś cāsya tribhir bāṇair mahārathaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Virāṭa struck Bhīṣma, that mighty car-warrior, with three arrows, and the great car-warrior pierced his horses with three arrows more.

sanskrit: taṃ pratyavidhyad daśabhir bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavaḥ śaraiḥ rukmapuṅkhair maheṣvāsaḥ kṛtahasto mahābalaḥ
english: In return Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, that mighty bowman of skilled hand and great strength, pierced him with ten gold-feathered shafts.

sanskrit: drauṇir gāṇḍīvadhanvānaṃ bhīmadhanvā mahārathaḥ avidhyad iṣubhiḥ ṣaḍbhir dṛḍhahastaḥ stanāntare
english: Droṇa's son, a great car-warrior of the dreadful bow and firm hand, struck the wielder of Gāṇḍīva with six arrows between the breasts.

sanskrit: kārmukaṃ tasya ciccheda phalgunaḥ paravīrahā avidhyac ca bhṛśaṃ tīkṣṇaiḥ patribhiḥ śatrukarśanaḥ
english: Phalguna, slayer of hostile heroes, cut his bow asunder, and that tormentor of foes pierced him sorely with sharp, feathered shafts.

sanskrit: so 'nyat kārmukam ādāya vegavat krodhamūrchitaḥ amṛṣyamāṇaḥ pārthena kārmukacchedam āhave
english: Unable to bear the cutting of his bow by Pārtha in the battle, and overpowered by wrath, he took up another swift-shooting bow.

sanskrit: avidhyat phalgunaṃ rājan navatyā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ vāsudevaṃ ca saptatyā vivyādha parameṣubhiḥ
english: He pierced Phalguna, O king, with ninety whetted arrows, and struck Vāsudeva with seventy excellent shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ krodhābhitāmrākṣaḥ saha kṛṣṇena phalgunaḥ dīrgham uṣṇaṃ ca niḥśvasya cintayitvā muhur muhuḥ
english: Then Phalguna, his eyes turned coppery with rage, together with Kṛṣṇa, drawing a long and burning breath and pondering again and again,

sanskrit: dhanuḥ prapīḍya vāmena kareṇāmitrakarśanaḥ gāṇḍīvadhanvā saṃkruddhaḥ śitān saṃnataparvaṇaḥ jīvitāntakarān ghorān samādatta śilīmukhān
english: That tormentor of enemies, the wrathful wielder of Gāṇḍīva, gripping his bow firm with his left hand, took up keen, well-jointed, dreadful arrows that bring life to its end.

sanskrit: tais tūrṇaṃ samare 'vidhyad drauṇiṃ balavatāṃ varam tasya te kavacaṃ bhittvā papuḥ śoṇitam āhave
english: With these he swiftly struck Droṇa's son, foremost of the strong, in battle; and piercing his armor, those shafts drank his blood in the fray.

sanskrit: na vivyathe ca nirbhinno drauṇir gāṇḍīvadhanvanā tathaiva śaravarṣāṇi pratimuñcann avihvalaḥ tasthau sa samare rājaṃs trātum icchan mahāvratam
english: Yet though pierced by the wielder of Gāṇḍīva, Droṇa's son did not waver; unshaken, hurling back showers of arrows, he stood firm in the fight, O king, wishing to protect Bhīṣma of the great vow.

sanskrit: tasya tat sumahat karma śaśaṃsuḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ yat kṛṣṇābhyāṃ sametābhyāṃ nāpatrapata saṃyuge
english: The bulls among men praised that mighty deed of his, that he was not abashed in combat before the two Kṛṣṇas joined together.

sanskrit: sa hi nityam anīkeṣu yudhyate 'bhayam āsthitaḥ astragrāmaṃ sasaṃhāraṃ droṇāt prāpya sudurlabham
english: For ever in the ranks he fought, established in fearlessness, having obtained from Droṇa the whole array of weapons with their withdrawal, a thing most hard to gain.

sanskrit: mamāyam ācāryasuto droṇasyātipriyaḥ sutaḥ brāhmaṇaś ca viśeṣeṇa mānanīyo mameti ca
english: "This man is the son of my teacher, the dearly beloved son of Droṇa, and a brāhmaṇa besides, and so to be especially honored by me" —

sanskrit: samāsthāya matiṃ vīro bībhatsuḥ śatrutāpanaḥ kṛpāṃ cakre rathaśreṣṭho bhāradvājasutaṃ prati
english: forming this resolve, the heroic Bībhatsu, scorcher of foes, foremost of car-warriors, showed mercy toward the son of Bhāradvāja's line.

sanskrit: drauṇiṃ tyaktvā tato yuddhe kaunteyaḥ śatrutāpanaḥ yuyudhe tāvakān nighnaṃs tvaramāṇaḥ parākramī
english: Leaving Droṇa's son alone, then, the valiant son of Kuntī, scorcher of foes, fought on, swiftly slaying your warriors.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu daśabhir gārdhrapatraiḥ śilāśitaiḥ bhīmasenaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ rukmapuṅkhaiḥ samarpayat
english: But Duryodhana assailed the mighty bowman Bhīmasena with ten vulture-feathered, gold-nocked arrows whetted on stone.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu saṃkruddhaḥ parāsukaraṇaṃ dṛḍham citraṃ kārmukam ādatta śarāṃś ca niśitān daśa
english: Then Bhīmasena, filled with wrath, took up a stout and gaily-wrought bow, a destroyer of foes, and ten whetted arrows.

sanskrit: ākarṇaprahitais tīkṣṇair vegitais tigmatejanaiḥ avidhyat tūrṇam avyagraḥ kururājaṃ mahorasi
english: With sharp, swift, fiercely glowing shafts drawn back to the ear, the unfaltering one quickly struck the king of the Kurus on his broad chest.

sanskrit: tasya kāñcanasūtras tu śaraiḥ parivṛto maṇiḥ rarājorasi vai sūryo grahair iva samāvṛtaḥ
english: The jewel on its golden chain, ringed about by those arrows, shone upon his breast like the sun encircled by the planets.

sanskrit: putras tu tava tejasvī bhīmasenena tāḍitaḥ nāmṛṣyata yathā nāgas talaśabdaṃ samīritam
english: But your splendid son, struck by Bhīmasena, brooked it no more than an elephant brooks the sound of a clapped palm raised against it.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarair mahārāja rukmapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ bhīmaṃ vivyādha saṃkruddhas trāsayāno varūthinīm
english: Then, O great king, full of wrath and striking terror into the host, he pierced Bhīma with gold-nocked arrows whetted on stone.

sanskrit: tau yudhyamānau samare bhṛśam anyonyavikṣatau putrau te devasaṃkāśau vyarocetāṃ mahābalau
english: As they fought in battle, sorely wounding each other, those two mighty sons of yours, godlike, shone resplendent.

sanskrit: citrasenaṃ naravyāghraṃ saubhadraḥ paravīrahā avidhyad daśabhir bāṇaiḥ purumitraṃ ca saptabhiḥ
english: Subhadrā's son, that slayer of hostile heroes, pierced Citrasena, the tiger among men, with ten arrows, and Purumitra with seven.

sanskrit: satyavrataṃ ca saptatyā viddhvā śakrasamo yudhi nṛtyann iva raṇe vīra ārtiṃ naḥ samajījanat
english: And piercing Satyavrata with seventy, that hero, equal to Śakra in war, as though dancing in the fray, begot anguish in us.

sanskrit: taṃ pratyavidyad daśabhiś citrasenaḥ śilīmukhaiḥ satyavrataś ca navabhiḥ purumitraś ca saptabhiḥ
english: In return Citrasena struck him with ten shafts, Satyavrata with nine, and Purumitra with seven.

sanskrit: sa viddho vikṣaran raktaṃ śatrusaṃvāraṇaṃ mahat ciccheda citrasenasya citraṃ kārmukam ārjuniḥ bhittvā cāsya tanutrāṇaṃ śareṇorasy atāḍayat
english: Pierced and streaming blood, the son of Arjuna cut Citrasena's great gaily-wrought bow, that warder-off of foes, and breaking through his armor, struck him on the breast with a shaft.

sanskrit: tatas te tāvakā vīrā rājaputrā mahārathāḥ sametya yudhi saṃrabdhā vivyadhur niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ tāṃś ca sarvāñ śarais tīkṣṇair jaghāna paramāstravit
english: Then your heroic warriors, the princes, great car-warriors, joining together in fury, pierced him with whetted arrows; but he, knowing the highest weapons, smote them all with sharp shafts.

sanskrit: tasya dṛṣṭvā tu tat karma parivavruḥ sutās tava dahantaṃ samare sainyaṃ tava kakṣaṃ yatholbaṇam
english: Beholding that deed of his, your sons surrounded him, as he burned your army in battle like a raging fire consuming dry grass.

sanskrit: apetaśiśire kāle samiddham iva pāvakaḥ atyarocata saubhadras tava sainyāni śātayan
english: Like a blazing fire when the cold season is past, the son of Subhadrā shone surpassingly bright as he cut down your troops.

sanskrit: tat tasya caritaṃ dṛṣṭvā pautras tava viśāṃ pate lakṣmaṇo 'bhyapatat tūrṇaṃ sātvatīputram āhave
english: Beholding that exploit of his, O lord of peoples, your grandson Lakṣmaṇa swiftly fell upon the son of the Sātvata princess in battle.

sanskrit: abhimanyus tu saṃkruddho lakṣmaṇaṃ śubhalakṣaṇam vivyādha viśikhaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ sārathiṃ ca tribhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: But Abhimanyu, filled with wrath, pierced Lakṣmaṇa of auspicious marks with six shafts, and his charioteer with three arrows.

sanskrit: tathaiva lakṣmaṇo rājan saubhadraṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ avidhyata mahārāja tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: In the same way Lakṣmaṇa, O king, struck the son of Subhadrā with whetted arrows; and that, O great king, seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: tasyāśvāṃś caturo hatvā sārathiṃ ca mahābalaḥ abhyadravata saubhadro lakṣmaṇaṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Having slain his four horses and his charioteer, the mighty son of Subhadrā rushed upon Lakṣmaṇa with whetted arrows.

sanskrit: hatāśve tu rathe tuṣṭhaṃl lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā śaktiṃ cikṣepa saṃkruddhaḥ saubhadrasya rathaṃ prati
english: Standing upon his car whose horses were slain, Lakṣmaṇa, slayer of hostile heroes, in his wrath hurled a spear at the chariot of Subhadrā's son.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā ghorarūpāṃ durāsadām abhimanyuḥ śarais tīkṣṇaiś ciccheda bhujagopamām
english: As it sped suddenly upon him, dreadful of form, hard to withstand, and like a serpent, Abhimanyu cut it apart with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ svaratham āropya lakṣmaṇaṃ gautamas tadā apovāha rathenājau sarvasainyasya paśyataḥ
english: Then Gautama, taking Lakṣmaṇa up onto his own car, bore him away from the battle in his chariot before the eyes of all the host.

sanskrit: tataḥ samākule tasmin vartamāne mahābhaye abhyadravañ jighāṃsantaḥ parasparavadhaiṣiṇaḥ
english: Then, in that great and terrible tumult that prevailed, they rushed at one another, eager to kill, each seeking the other's death.

sanskrit: tāvakāś ca maheṣvāsāḥ pāṇḍavāś ca mahārathāḥ juhvantaḥ samare prāṇān nijaghnur itaretaram
english: Your mighty bowmen and the great car-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas, offering up their very lives in the battle, slew one another.

sanskrit: muktakeśā vikavacā virathāś chinnakārmukāḥ bāhubhiḥ samayudhyanta sṛñjayāḥ kurubhiḥ saha
english: Their hair loosened, their armor gone, bereft of chariots and their bows cut to pieces, the Sṛñjayas fought with the Kurus with their bare arms.

sanskrit: tato bhīṣmo mahābāhuḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām senāṃ jaghāna saṃkruddho divyair astrair mahābalaḥ
english: Then mighty-armed Bhīṣma of great strength, full of wrath, smote the army of the high-souled Pāṇḍavas with celestial weapons.

sanskrit: hateśvarair gajais tatra narair aśvaiś ca pātitaiḥ rathibhiḥ sādibhiś caiva samāstīryata medinī
english: There the earth was strewn over with elephants whose riders were slain, with men and fallen horses, with car-warriors and horsemen alike.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca atha rājan mahābāhuḥ sātyakir yuddhadurmadaḥ vikṛṣya cāpaṃ samare bhārasādhanam uttamam
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, O king, mighty-armed Sātyaki, frenzied in war, drawing in the battle his bow, that excellent accomplisher of heavy tasks,

sanskrit: prāmuñcat puṅkhasaṃyuktāñ śarān āśīviṣopamān prakāśaṃ laghu citraṃ ca darśayann astralāghavam
english: loosed well-feathered shafts like venomous serpents, displaying clear, swift, and dazzling lightness of hand with his weapons.

sanskrit: tasya vikṣipataś cāpaṃ śarān anyāṃś ca muñcataḥ ādadānasya bhūyaś ca saṃdadhānasya cāparān
english: As he flexed his bow and loosed yet other arrows, and again took up more and set still others to the string,

sanskrit: kṣipataś ca śarān asya raṇe śatrūn vinighnataḥ dadṛśe rūpam atyarthaṃ meghasyeva pravarṣataḥ
english: and hurled his shafts and slew the foe in the fray, his form appeared exceedingly like a cloud pouring down rain.

sanskrit: tam udīryantam ālokya rājā duryodhanas tataḥ rathānām ayutaṃ tasya preṣayām āsa bhārata
english: Beholding him thus rising in fury, king Duryodhana then sent against him ten thousand chariots, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu sarvān maheṣvāsān sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ jaghāna parameṣvāso divyenāstreṇa vīryavān
english: But Sātyaki of true valor, the supreme bowman of great might, slew all those mighty archers with a celestial weapon.

sanskrit: sa kṛtvā dāruṇaṃ karma pragṛhītaśarāsanaḥ āsasāda tato vīro bhūriśravasam āhave
english: Having wrought that dreadful deed, the hero, his bow grasped firmly, then closed with Bhūriśravas in the battle.

sanskrit: sa hi saṃdṛśya senāṃ tāṃ yuyudhānena pātitām abhyadhāvata saṃkruddhaḥ kurūṇāṃ kīrtivardhanaḥ
english: For he, that increaser of the Kurus' fame, beholding that host laid low by Yuyudhāna, charged at him in wrath.

sanskrit: indrāyudhasavarṇaṃ tat sa visphārya mahad dhanuḥ vyasṛjad vajrasaṃkāśāñ śarān āśīviṣopamān sahasraśo mahārāja darśayan pāṇilāghavam
english: Twanging that great bow colored like Indra's bow, the rainbow, he loosed shafts resembling the thunderbolt and like venomous serpents by the thousand, O great king, displaying the lightness of his hand.

sanskrit: śarāṃs tān mṛtyusaṃsparśān sātyakes tu padānugāḥ na viṣehus tadā rājan dudruvus te samantataḥ vihāya samare rājan sātyakiṃ yuddhadurmadam
english: Those arrows whose touch was death the followers of Sātyaki could not endure, O king; they fled in every direction, abandoning in the battle, O king, Sātyaki frenzied in war.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā yuyudhānasya sutā daśa mahābalāḥ mahārathāḥ samākhyātāś citravarmāyudhadhvajāḥ
english: Seeing this, the ten mighty sons of Yuyudhāna, renowned great car-warriors with brilliant armor, weapons, and banners,

sanskrit: samāsādya maheṣvāsaṃ bhūriśravasam āhave ūcuḥ sarve susaṃrabdhā yūpaketuṃ mahāraṇe
english: closing in battle with the mighty bowman Bhūriśravas, all in great fury addressed him whose banner bore the sacrificial post, in that great fray:

sanskrit: bho bho kauravadāyāda sahāsmābhir mahābala ehi yudhyasva saṃgrāme samastaiḥ pṛthag eva vā
english: "Ho, ho, heir of the Kauravas, O mighty one! Come, fight with us in battle, with all of us together or with each one apart.

sanskrit: asmān vā tvaṃ parājitya yaśaḥ prāpnuhi saṃyuge vayaṃ vā tvāṃ parājitya prītiṃ dāsyāmahe pituḥ
english: Either vanquish us and win glory in combat, or we, vanquishing you, shall give joy to our father."

sanskrit: evam uktas tadā śūrais tān uvāca mahābalaḥ vīryaślāghī naraśreṣṭhas tān dṛṣṭvā samupasthitān
english: Thus addressed by those heroes, the mighty one, foremost of men, who gloried in valor, beholding them drawn up before him, said to them:

sanskrit: sādhv idaṃ kathyate vīrā yad evaṃ matir adya vaḥ yudhyadhvaṃ sahitā yattā nihaniṣyāmi vo raṇe
english: "Well is this spoken, O heroes, that such is your resolve this day. Fight all together, intent upon it; I shall slay you in the battle."

sanskrit: evam uktā maheṣvāsās te vīrāḥ kṣiprakāriṇaḥ mahatā śaravarṣeṇa abhyavarṣann ariṃdamam
english: Thus addressed, those heroic, swift-handed bowmen rained upon that tamer of foes a mighty shower of arrows.

sanskrit: aparāhṇe mahārāja saṃgrāmas tumulo 'bhavat ekasya ca bahūnāṃ ca sametānāṃ raṇājire
english: In the afternoon, O great king, a tumultuous combat arose on the field of battle between the one and the many assembled together.

sanskrit: tam ekaṃ rathināṃ śreṣṭhaṃ śaravarṣair avākiran prāvṛṣīva mahāśailaṃ siṣicur jaladā nṛpa
english: That one, foremost of car-warriors, they covered over with showers of arrows, as in the rains the clouds drench a great mountain, O king.

sanskrit: tais tu muktāñ śaraughāṃs tān yamadaṇḍāśaniprabhān asaṃprāptān asaṃprāptāṃś cicchedāśu mahārathaḥ
english: But the floods of arrows loosed by them, gleaming like the rod of Yama and the thunderbolt, that great car-warrior swiftly cut to pieces ere they reached him, again and again before they came.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma saumadatteḥ parākramam yad eko bahubhir yuddhe samasajjad abhītavat
english: There we beheld a marvel, the prowess of Somadatta's son, that he alone closed in battle with the many, undaunted.

sanskrit: visṛjya śaravṛṣṭiṃ tāṃ daśa rājan mahārathāḥ parivārya mahābāhuṃ nihantum upacakramuḥ
english: Having poured forth that rain of arrows, the ten great car-warriors, O king, surrounded the mighty-armed one and set about to slay him.

sanskrit: saumadattis tataḥ kruddhas teṣāṃ cāpāni bhārata ciccheda daśabhir bāṇair nimeṣeṇa mahārathaḥ
english: Then the son of Somadatta, in wrath, that great car-warrior, O descendant of Bharata, cut their bows asunder with ten arrows in the twinkling of an eye.

sanskrit: athaiṣāṃ chinnadhanuṣāṃ bhallaiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ ciccheda samare rājañ śirāṃsi niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ te hatā nyapatan bhūmau vajrabhagnā iva drumāḥ
english: Then, their bows broken, he cut off their heads in the battle, O king, with whetted, well-jointed broad-headed shafts; slain, they fell to the earth like trees shattered by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā nihatān vīrān raṇe putrān mahābalān vārṣṇeyo vinadan rājan bhūriśravasam abhyayāt
english: Seeing those heroes, his mighty sons, slain in the battle, the Vārṣṇeya, roaring aloud, O king, rushed at Bhūriśravas.

sanskrit: rathaṃ rathena samare pīḍayitvā mahābalau tāv anyonyasya samare nihatya rathavājinaḥ virathāv abhivalgantau sameyātāṃ mahārathau
english: Pressing car against car in the battle, those two mighty ones, having each slain the other's chariot-horses in the fray, met together, those great car-warriors, leaping forward, both bereft of their cars.

sanskrit: pragṛhītamahākhaḍgau tau carmavaradhāriṇau śuśubhāte naravyāghrau yuddhāya samavasthitau
english: Grasping their great swords and bearing their excellent shields, those two tigers among men shone resplendent as they took their stand for combat.

sanskrit: tataḥ sātyakim abhyetya nistriṃśavaradhāriṇam bhīmasenas tvaran rājan ratham āropayat tadā
english: Then Bhīmasena, hastening up to Sātyaki who bore his excellent sword, mounted him upon his car at that time, O king.

sanskrit: tavāpi tanayo rājan bhūriśravasam āhave āropayad rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ paśyatāṃ sarvadhanvinām
english: And your son too, O king, swiftly mounted Bhūriśravas upon a chariot in the battle, before the eyes of all the bowmen.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tathā vartamāne raṇe bhīṣmaṃ mahāratham ayodhayanta saṃrabdhāḥ pāṇḍavā bharatarṣabha
english: While that combat thus went on, the Pāṇḍavas in their fury did battle with Bhīṣma, the great car-warrior, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: lohitāyati cāditye tvaramāṇo dhanaṃjayaḥ pañcaviṃśatisāhasrān nijaghāna mahārathān
english: As the sun grew red, Dhanaṃjaya, making haste, slew twenty-five thousand great car-warriors.

sanskrit: te hi duryodhanādiṣṭās tadā pārthanibarhaṇe saṃprāpyaiva gatā nāśaṃ śalabhā iva pāvakam
english: For these, commanded by Duryodhana then to the destruction of Pārtha, went to their ruin as soon as they reached him, like moths into a flame.

sanskrit: tato matsyāḥ kekayāś ca dhanurvedaviśāradāḥ parivavrus tadā pārthaṃ sahaputraṃ mahāratham
english: Then the Matsyas and the Kekayas, skilled in the science of the bow, surrounded Pārtha, that great car-warrior, together with his son.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu sūrye 'stam upagacchati sarveṣām eva sainyānāṃ pramohaḥ samajāyata
english: At that very time, as the sun was going down to its setting, a bewilderment came over all the troops alike.

sanskrit: avahāraṃ tataś cakre pitā devavratas tava saṃdhyākāle mahārāja sainyānāṃ śrāntavāhanaḥ
english: Then your father Devavrata, O great king, at the hour of twilight, called off the troops, their mounts grown weary.
